title: Demo Day Dry Runs - Notes (Week 1-3)
body:
Doc intent: running notes from internal “Standard Demo v1” dry runs (weeks 1–3). Capture what broke + where narrative is confusing + timing + concrete action items.

Owner: Talia (program mgmt). Please add notes inline; action items should be explicit with owner + due date.

======
Context / what we’re practicing
- Audience/personas: Platform Eng lead, ML Eng lead, Security/Compliance
- Format: 25–30 min standard demo + 10–15 min Q&A
- “Must show” differentiators:
  1) Reliable production inference (latency, throughput consistency)
  2) Cost controls (batching/caching/quotization profiles + token cost visibility)
  3) Reliability + graceful degradation (routing + fallback)
  4) Deployment flexibility (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private narrative)
  5) Observability (route dashboards, error analysis, rollouts)

Known “demo tenant” constraints
- No customer data, no PII; use canned prompts only.
- Prefer deterministic-ish outputs: use pinned model versions + seeded prompts + show expected output snippet.
- Always have Plan B (screenshots / prerecorded JSON / dashboard export) if live systems degrade.

======
Week 1 – Dry Run #1 (kickoff / baseline)
Date: 2025-08-06
Target persona: Platform Eng (technical buyer)
Driver: Markus (Console + API). Narrator: Soojin.
Attendees: Markus, Soojin, Simran, Colin, Logan, Chloe, Marissa, Talia.

Run-of-show (actual): 38 min demo + 12 min Q&A (too long)
- 0:00–0:04 intro + “why serving matters” (good)
- 0:04–0:14 Hosted API quickstart (ok, but too many steps)
- 0:14–0:24 Console: routes + dashboards (confusing click path)
- 0:24–0:33 Routing/fallback live test (worked but narration unclear)
- 0:33–0:38 Dedicated/Private positioning (felt bolted-on)

What landed well
- Showing streaming response early (people immediately get “app feel”).
- Cost dashboard concept resonates, but we didn’t get to a crisp “before/after” story.
- Fallback demo is compelling when we explain it as “policy + automated compatibility” vs “manual knob”.

What broke / issues
1) Console clickpath confusion
- We lost ~2 minutes finding the saved dashboard view (wrong nav section). People in room unsure where to look.
- Action: create a “Demo Saved Views” section in Console (or at least consistent naming). If product change too heavy, create a doc + pinned URL shortcuts.
  - Owner: Chloe + Marissa
  - Due: 2025-08-13

2) Dashboard lag
- Cost panel updated ~60–90 sec after request; in live demo that feels like “nothing happened”.
- Workaround used: refresh manually + narrate “pipeline delay”. Didn’t sound confident.
- Action: add a “last updated” timestamp and/or guidance in talk track: “cost panels are aggregated; for live requests, use the trace view first.”
  - Owner: Logan (telemetry) + Soojin (talk track)
  - Due: 2025-08-15

3) Unclear narrative on batching/caching
- We said “we do batching/caching” but didn’t show what the customer controls.
- Action: add one slide (or one Console screenshot) that shows the knobs + the impact metric (e.g., tokens/sec, $/1M tokens). Avoid hard numbers; show relative change.
  - Owner: Soojin
  - Due: 2025-08-16

4) Too many “setup-ish” steps in quickstart
- We spent too long on auth/env vars + copying curl commands.
- Action: have a single “copy-paste” request that works out of box + one pre-filled Postman/Insomnia collection.
  - Owner: Renee (enablement) + Colin
  - Due: 2025-08-19

Confusing sections (callouts)
- Transition Hosted -> Dedicated: we jumped straight to “reserved GPUs” without first summarizing why (predictability + data isolation + SLAs).
- Need a single sentence: “Same API; Dedicated just changes the capacity + isolation layer.”
  - Owner: Soojin

Decisions / changes proposed
- Move “fallback” earlier (right after basic request) for platform persona.
- Keep Private narrative as optional branch; do not always do full Private walkthrough in standard 30 min.

Action item summary (Week 1)
- [Chloe/Marissa] Create consistent saved views / pinned URLs for demo dashboards.
- [Logan/Soojin] Fix talk track for dashboard lag + show trace-first.
- [Soojin] Add one “cost knobs” slide/screenshot.
- [Renee/Colin] Reduce quickstart friction (single copy-paste request + optional client).

======
Week 2 – Dry Run #2 (security-focused)
Date: 2025-08-13
Target persona: Security + Compliance
Driver: Markus. Narrator: Naomi (security FAQ) + Soojin (narrative).
Attendees: Naomi, Markus, Soojin, Rafael, Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei, Talia, Sean.

Goal for this run
- Prove we can handle security Q&A without derailing demo.
- Validate “demo tenant is safe” positioning (no sensitive data, access controls, logging posture).

Run-of-show (actual): 29 min demo + 25 min Q&A (Q&A blew up)
- We stayed too long in Q&A because answers weren’t crisp and we hunted for exact wording.

Security questions that came up (capture exact phrasing)
1) “Are you training on our data?”
- We answered correctly but too many caveats.
- Needs a standard 15-second answer: “No training on customer prompts by default; configurable retention; contract + controls. For demo tenant specifically: prompts are canned + sanitized; retention is minimal and access-controlled.”
  - Owner: Naomi + Marcus Lin

2) “What gets logged? Can we turn off logging?”
- We said “audit logs exist” but didn’t separate: request logs vs platform audit logs.
- Action: update security FAQ to explicitly distinguish:
  - inference request/response logging (configurable)
  - metadata metrics/traces (token counts, timings)
  - admin/audit events (policy changes, key rotations, user access)
  - Owner: Kevin + Naomi
  - Due: 2025-08-20

3) “SSO/SAML and RBAC support?”
- We hand-waved: “yes enterprise SSO.” Need exact feature list + what demo tenant uses.
- Action: add a 1-slide appendix for security persona: SSO/SAML, RBAC roles, SCIM (if applicable), and how access is managed internally for demo tenant.
  - Owner: Naomi + Soojin
  - Due: 2025-08-22

4) “Data residency / EU routing”
- Question: “If we need EU-only processing, can you guarantee it?”
- We did not have a crisp answer in the talk track.
- Decision (for now): in standard demo, say “region pinning available; for strict residency we scope it in eval/POC; demo tenant default is US, but we can discuss EU-only setups in Dedicated/Private.”
  - Owner: Lukas (EMEA input) + Soojin

What broke / issues
1) Demo tenant login/access friction (internal)
- Markus had to re-auth once mid-demo (SSO session expired). It killed momentum.
- Action: pre-demo checklist item: re-login 10 min before start + keep a “driver-only” browser profile.
  - Owner: Markus + Rafael

2) We lacked a “safe statement” list
- We kept circling on whether we can say SOC2, retention durations, etc.
- Action: compile “approved security language for demos” (1 page) referencing the Security FAQ. Keep it internal.
  - Owner: Naomi
  - Due: 2025-08-23

Timing / narrative fixes
- For security persona, skip cost dashboard live unless asked. Keep the story: isolation + controls + auditability.
- Add explicit “demo tenant vs production deployment” separation early:
  - “Demo tenant is sanitized and locked down; production deployments are configurable to your policies.”

Plan B assets needed
- “Security appendix” slide(s)
- One screenshot of audit log view (with fake events)
- One screenshot of RBAC roles page (sanitized)

Action item summary (Week 2)
- [Kevin/Naomi] Clarify logging vs audit logs in FAQ.
- [Naomi/Soojin] Add security appendix slides + approved language page.
- [Markus/Rafael] Add pre-demo login/SSO sanity step to checklist.
- [Soojin/Lukas] Tighten data residency answer + branch guidance.

======
Week 3 – Dry Run #3 (routing/fallback + Dedicated)
Date: 2025-08-20
Target persona: Platform Eng + procurement-adjacent (reliability/SLA)
Driver: Markus. Narrator: Soojin. Support: Mina (routing), Sean (SRE).
Attendees: Mina Haddad, Sean Gallagher, Markus Klein, Soojin Lee, Logan Wright, Chloe Martin, Talia.

Goal for this run
- Nail the “graceful degradation” story and prove it live.
- Show Dedicated upgrade path without over-promising on exact SLA numbers.

Run-of-show (actual): 33 min demo + 15 min Q&A
- Better, but still over 30 min due to troubleshooting a throttling moment.

What worked
- The “policy routing” explanation improved when Mina framed it as:
  - “Requests are classified and routed by policy; fallbacks are pre-validated compatible variants; we can choose ‘keep latency’ vs ‘keep cost’.”
- Dedicated story improved when we anchored it to:
  - predictability, isolation, and “no surprise throttles” (for committed capacity)

What broke / issues
1) Throttling/429 confusion during live scenario
- We hit a 429 briefly (likely quota window from prior tests).
- It derailed the story because we didn’t say whether it was expected.
- Action: in reset checklist, include “clear recent load / verify quota headroom” and a quick “/limits” check call.
  - Owner: Cole Summers (quota) + Rafael
  - Due: 2025-08-27
- Action: talk track: when a 429 occurs, say:
  - “This is the shared demo tenant’s safety rail; in Dedicated you get reserved throughput and dedicated limits.”
  - Owner: Soojin

2) Fallback demo steps too fragile
- We toggled a routing rule live; the UI took a moment to apply; we weren’t sure if the request used old policy.
- Action: define one deterministic “failure-mode trigger” that doesn’t rely on last-second UI toggles (e.g., route-specific header or a prepared canary rule).
  - Owner: Mina + Marissa
  - Due: 2025-08-29

3) Error analysis view was hard to interpret
- We opened an error panel and it was empty (because timeframe default was 24h; our requests were last 5 min).
- Action: set demo saved views with timeframe pinned (last 15 min) + add “timeframe” reminder in clickpath notes.
  - Owner: Chloe

4) “Dedicated SLA” questions
- Q: “What SLA do you offer?” We danced around it (we should).
- Decision: no explicit SLA numbers in standard deck. Use phrasing:
  - “SLA-backed uptime/latency targets are available; specifics depend on region/model/capacity tier; we’ll share in a commercial follow-up.”
  - Owner: Soojin + Markus (objection handling notes)

Narrative sections still confusing
- We still have an awkward jump from “fallback” to “observability”. The bridge should be:
  - “Because routing is policy-driven, you need visibility. Here’s how we observe route-level latency/cost/errors, and how you prove the policy is working.”
  - Owner: Soojin

Plan B / hardening ideas
- If routing toggle doesn’t apply, have a pre-recorded curl output that shows:
  - response headers indicating selected backend/model variant
  - trace ID linking to Console trace view
- If dashboards lag, show trace first, then return to aggregated dashboards.

Action item summary (Week 3)
- [Cole/Rafael] Add quota headroom verification to reset checklist.
- [Mina/Marissa] Make fallback trigger deterministic (avoid fragile UI toggles).
- [Chloe] Fix saved view default timeframes.
- [Soojin/Markus] Update Dedicated SLA safe-language in objection notes.

======
Cross-week themes (what keeps biting us)
1) Demo reliability is mostly “demo hygiene”
- Logging in ahead of time, resetting quotas, pinning timeframes, having saved views.
- We need the checklist to be the ritual.

2) Console clickpath needs to be scripted
- “Driver notes” should include exact clicks + deep links.
- Consider one printed page for drivers.

3) Avoid live edits
- Live toggling rules/policies is high-risk unless it’s designed for demos.
- Better: have pre-created routes and just send requests to specific endpoints that demonstrate the behavior.

4) Don’t over-index on metrics
- Prospects ask for numbers, but live demos are not benchmarking.
- We need credible “ranges” and focus on the controls + observability.

======
Open questions
- Do we need a 2-minute “Hosted API mini-demo” variant (no Console) for first calls? (see Slack sales thread)
- For EMEA: do we create an EU-only demo tenant, or keep it as a Dedicated/Private story only?
- Should the standard demo include tool calling by default, or keep it as an ML Eng branch?

======
Next steps before field rollout
- Convert these notes into:
  - Updated talk track (speaker notes)
  - Updated reset checklist (pre/post)
  - Updated “known-good scenario matrix” with regression status
  - A single “driver script” with links + Plan B assets

If you add new issues here, please also add the corresponding ticket (Linear preferred) and link it above.
